title.zh: 卷46 列傳第11 趙煚 趙芬 楊尚希 長孫平 元暉 韋師 楊异 蘇孝慈 李雄 張煚
title.en: Volume 46 Biographies 11: Zhao Jiong, Zhao Fen, Yang shangxi, Zhang Sunping, Yuan Hui, Wei Shi, Yang Yi, Su Xiaoci, Li Xiong, Zhang Jiong
title.raw: 卷46 列傳第11 趙煚 趙芬 楊尚希 長孫平 元暉 韋師 楊异 蘇孝慈 李雄 張煚 Volume 46 Biographies 11: Zhao Jiong, Zhao Fen, Yang shangxi, Zhang Sunping, Yuan Hui, Wei Shi, Yang Yi, Su Xiaoci, Li Xiong, Zhang Jiong

sentences.zh: 隋書卷四十六列傳第十一

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume Forty-Six, Biographies Eleven
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 46, Biographies 11

sentences.zh: 趙煚，字賢通，天水西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Jiong, style name Xiantong, was a man of Western Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jiong, whose style name was Xiantong, came from Western Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 祖超宗，魏河東太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chaozong was Administrator of Hedong in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chaozong had served as Administrator of Hedong under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父仲懿，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His father Zhongyi was Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongyi had been Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 煚少孤，養母至孝。

translations.literal: Jiong lost his father while young and nursed his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was orphaned in youth and cared for his mother with exemplary devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十四，有人盜伐其父墓中樹者，煚對之號慟，因執送官。

translations.literal: At age fourteen, when someone stole and cut trees from his father's tomb, Jiong wailed before him in grief and had him seized and sent to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, when he found someone felling trees in his father's grave, he wept aloud in anguish before the man and had him handed over to the officials.

sentences.zh: 見魏右僕射周惠達，長揖不拜，自述孤苦，涕泗交集，惠達為之隕涕，歎息者久之。

translations.literal: When he met the Wei Right Vice Director Zhou Huida, he made a long bow without performing the full prostration, described his orphaned hardship, and tears mingled; Huida shed tears for him and sighed for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Zhou Huida, Right Vice Director of the Wei court, he gave a deep bow without kneeling, poured out his lonely plight until tears streamed down his face, and Huida wept in sympathy and sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 及長，深沉有器局，略涉書史。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was deep and reserved with capacity and vision, and had dipped slightly into books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he proved grave and far-sighted, with a measure of learning in history and the classics.

sentences.zh: 周太祖引為相府參軍事。

translations.literal: The Zhou Founder drew him in as Staff Officer of the Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Founder Yuwen Tai appointed him staff officer in the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 尋從破洛陽。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed in the capture of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took part in the campaign that captured Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及太祖班師，煚請留撫納亡叛，太祖從之。

translations.literal: When the Founder withdrew the army, Jiong requested to remain to pacify and accept deserters and rebels, and the Founder followed this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder withdrew his forces, Jiong asked to stay behind to win over deserters and rebels, and the Founder agreed.

sentences.zh: 煚於是帥所領與齊人前後五戰，斬郡守、鎮將、縣令五人，虜獲甚眾，以功封平定縣男，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Jiong thereupon led those under his command in five battles with the Qi, before and after, beheading five prefects, garrison commanders, and county magistrates, and capturing many; for merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingding County with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops through five engagements with Qi forces, killing five prefects, garrison commanders, and county magistrates and taking a great number captive; for these deeds he was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingding, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 累轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 閔帝受禪，遷陝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min accepted the abdication, Jiong was moved to Governor of Shan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min took the throne, he was appointed Governor of Shan Province.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋向天王聚眾作亂，以兵攻信陵、秭歸。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftain Xiang Tianwang gathered a host and made rebellion, attacking Xinling and Zigui with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chieftain Xiang Tianwang raised a rebel force and marched against Xinling and Zigui.

sentences.zh: 煚勒所部五百人，出其不意，襲擊破之，二郡獲全。

translations.literal: Jiong urged five hundred men of his command, taking them unawares, to strike and defeat them, and the two commanderies were preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong led five hundred of his men in a surprise attack that routed the rebels and saved both commanderies.

sentences.zh: 時周人於江南岸置安蜀城以禦陳，屬霖雨數旬，城頹者百余步。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou had set up Ancheng on the south bank of the Yangzi to resist Chen; it happened that rain fell for several tens of days, and more than a hundred paces of the wall collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou had built Ancheng on the southern bank of the Yangzi to hold Chen at bay, but weeks of heavy rain caused more than a hundred paces of the wall to crumble.

sentences.zh: 蠻酋鄭南鄉叛，引陳將吳明徹欲掩安蜀。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftain Zheng Nanxiang rebelled and brought in the Chen general Wu Mingche intending to seize Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal leader Zheng Nanxiang revolted and enlisted the Chen general Wu Mingche for a strike against Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 議者皆觀煚益修守禦，煚曰：「不然，吾自有以安之。」

translations.literal: Those in council all looked to Jiong to repair the defenses further; Jiong said, "It is not so—I have my own means to secure it."
translations.idiomatic: Counselors urged Jiong to strengthen the fortifications, but he said, "No—I have my own way to secure the place."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使說誘江外生蠻向武陽，令乘虛掩襲所居，獲其南鄉父母妻子。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to persuade and entice the raw barbarians beyond the river, Xiang Wuyang, to strike by surprise at Nanxiang's dwelling when he was absent, and seized Nanxiang's father, mother, wife, and children.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to win over Xiang Wuyang, a raw tribe beyond the river, and had him raid Nanxiang's home in his absence, capturing Nanxiang's parents, wife, and children.

sentences.zh: 南鄉聞之，其黨各散，陳兵遂退。

translations.literal: When Nanxiang heard of it, his partisans each scattered, and the Chen troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanxiang learned of this, his followers dispersed and the Chen army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，吳明徹屢為寇患，煚勒兵禦之，前後十六戰，每挫其鋒。

translations.literal: The next year Wu Mingche repeatedly made incursions; Jiong urged troops to resist him, sixteen battles before and after, each time blunting his edge.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wu Mingche raided repeatedly; Jiong met him in sixteen engagements and blunted his advance each time.

sentences.zh: 獲陳裨將覃冏、王足子、吳朗等三人，斬首百六十級。

translations.literal: He captured three Chen deputy generals, Tan Tong, Wang Zuzi, and Wu Lang, and took one hundred sixty heads.
translations.idiomatic: He captured three Chen deputy commanders—Tan Tong, Wang Zuzi, and Wu Lang—and took one hundred sixty heads.

sentences.zh: 以功授開府儀同三司，遷荊州總管長史。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted Opening the Office with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies and moved to Chief Clerk of the Jingzhou Grand Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was made a general of the third rank with full ceremonial honors and appointed chief clerk to the Jingzhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 入為民部中大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Grand Master of the Ministry of the People.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as a senior officer in the Ministry of the People.

sentences.zh: 武帝出兵鞏、洛，欲收齊河南之地。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu sent troops to Gong and Luo, wishing to recover the Qi lands south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu marched on Gong and Luoyang, aiming to recover Qi territory south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 煚諫曰：「河南洛陽，四面受敵，縱得之，不可以守。

translations.literal: Jiong remonstrated, saying, "Henan and Luoyang are attacked on all four sides; even if obtained, they cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong advised against it: "Luoyang in Henan is exposed on every side—even if we take it, we cannot hold it.

sentences.zh: 請從河北，直指太原，傾其巢穴，可一舉以定。」

translations.literal: I ask to advance from north of the river, strike straight at Taiyuan, overturn their nest, and in one move settle it."
translations.idiomatic: March from north of the river straight on Taiyuan and destroy their base—then the whole affair can be settled at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，師竟無功。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept this, and the army in the end achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected his counsel, and the campaign ended in failure.

sentences.zh: 尋從上柱國於翼率眾數萬，自三鴉道以伐陳，克陳十九城而還。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he followed the Pillar of State Yu Yi, leading several tens of thousands, by the Sanya route to attack Chen, captured nineteen Chen cities, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the pillar of state Yu Yi at the head of tens of thousands down the Sanya route against Chen, took nineteen cities, and returned.

sentences.zh: 以讒毀，功不見錄，除益州總管長史。

translations.literal: Because of slander his merit was not recorded, and he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Yizhou Grand Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Slander kept his achievements off the rolls, and he was made chief clerk of the Yizhou commandery instead.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為天官司會，累遷禦正上大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the capital as Director of the Bureau of Astronomy, and was transferred in succession to Senior Grand Master of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he returned to court as director of the Bureau of Astronomy and rose to senior grand master of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 煚與宗伯斛斯徵素不協，徵後出為齊州刺史，坐事下獄，自知罪重，遂逾獄而走。

translations.literal: Jiong and the Minister of the Imperial Clan Husizheng had long been at odds; Zheng later went out as Governor of Qi Province, was imprisoned for an offense, knew his guilt was heavy, and crossed the prison wall to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had long been at odds with Husizheng, Minister of the Imperial Clan; when Husizheng was later sent out as governor of Qi Province, imprisoned for an offense, and realized his guilt was grave, he broke out of jail and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，購之甚急。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and offered a reward for him with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and offered a rich bounty for his capture.

sentences.zh: 煚上密奏曰：「徵自以負罪深重，懼死遁逃，若不北竄匈奴，則南投吳越。

translations.literal: Jiong submitted a secret memorial, saying, "Zheng, considering himself burdened with deep guilt, fears death and flees; if he does not flee north to the Xiongnu, he will go south to Wu and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong sent a confidential memorial: "Knowing his guilt is grave, Husizheng fears execution and has fled—either north to the Xiongnu or south to Wu and Yue.

sentences.zh: 徵雖愚陋，久曆清顯，奔彼敵國，無益聖朝。

translations.literal: Although Zheng is foolish and base, he has long held clear and eminent office; to run to those enemy states would not benefit the holy court.
translations.idiomatic: For all his failings, he has long held high office; flight to an enemy state would do the court no good.

sentences.zh: 今者炎旱為災，可因茲大赦。」

translations.literal: Now drought and heat are calamities; one may take this occasion for a great amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: The land suffers drought and heat—this is an occasion for a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 徵賴而獲免，煚卒不言。

translations.literal: Zheng relied on this and obtained release; Jiong to the end did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Husizheng was spared by the amnesty, and Jiong never mentioned his own role.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，加上開府，複拜天官都司會。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, he was given the additional title of Opening the Office and was again appointed Director of the Bureau of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was still chancellor, Jiong was given the rank of opening the office and reappointed director of the Bureau of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 俄遷大宗伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Minister of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，煚授璽紱，進位大將軍，賜爵金城郡公，邑二千五百戶，拜相州刺史。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Jiong presented the seal and cord, was advanced to Grand General, was granted the title Duke of Jincheng Commandery with a fief of two thousand five hundred households, and was appointed Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty Jiong presented the imperial seal and cord, was promoted to grand general, enfeoffed as Duke of Jincheng with a fief of two thousand five hundred households, and appointed governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以煚曉習故事，征拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: The court, because Jiong was versed in precedent, summoned and appointed him Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, valuing his mastery of ritual and precedent.

sentences.zh: 視事未幾，以忤旨，尋出為陝州刺史，俄轉冀州刺史，甚有威德。

translations.literal: He had not long taken office when, for going against the imperial will, he was soon sent out as Governor of Shan Province, and shortly transferred to Governor of Ji Province, where he had great authority and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely taken up the post when he offended the throne and was sent out as governor of Shan, then soon transferred to Ji Province, where he ruled with great authority and moral force.

sentences.zh: 煚嘗有疾，百姓賓士，爭為祈禱，其得民情如此。

translations.literal: When Jiong once fell ill, commoners and guests alike vied to pray for him—such was his winning of the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, townspeople and visiting scholars alike prayed for his recovery—such was the affection he commanded.

sentences.zh: 冀州谷薄，市井多奸詐，煚為銅鬥鐵尺，置之于肆，百姓便之。

translations.literal: In Ji Province grain was scant and the markets had much fraud; Jiong made bronze bushels and iron rulers and placed them in the shops, and the people found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Province had short-weight grain and sharp dealing in the markets; Jiong provided standard bronze bushels and iron yardsticks for the shops, to the people's great relief.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉焉，頒告天下，以為常法。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and commended this, promulgated it throughout the realm, and made it a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the measure, proclaimed it empire-wide, and made it permanent law.

sentences.zh: 嘗有人盜煚田中蒿者，為吏所執。

translations.literal: Once someone stole artemisia from Jiong's fields and was seized by the clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Once a man was caught stealing wormwood from Jiong's fields.

sentences.zh: 煚曰：「此乃刺史不能宣風化，彼何罪也。」

translations.literal: Jiong said, "This is because the governor could not spread civilizing influence—what crime does he have?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said, "The fault lies with the governor, who has failed to teach the people—what crime has this man committed?

sentences.zh: 慰諭而遣之，令人載蒿一車以賜盜者。

translations.literal: He comforted and instructed him and sent him away, and had someone load a cart of artemisia to give to the thief.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted the man and let him go, then had a full cart of wormwood sent to him as a gift.

sentences.zh: 盜者愧恧，過於重刑。

translations.literal: The thief was ashamed and remorseful, more than if he had suffered heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The thief was more ashamed than if he had been heavily punished.

sentences.zh: 其以德化民，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His transforming the people through virtue was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His rule by moral example was of this kind throughout.

sentences.zh: 上幸洛陽，煚來朝，上勞之曰：「冀州大籓，民用殷實，卿之為政，深副朕懷。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited Luoyang, Jiong came to court; the Emperor comforted him, saying, "Ji is a great frontier province, its people prosperous and solid—your administration deeply matches Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Luoyang, Jiong came to court and was told, "Ji is a great border province whose people are thriving—your governance has fully satisfied my expectations.

sentences.zh: 開皇十九年卒，時年六十八。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kaihuang he died, at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year of Kaihuang, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子義臣嗣，官至太子洗馬。

translations.literal: His son Yichen succeeded him and reached the office of Groom of the Heir Apparent's Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yichen succeeded him and rose to groom in the heir apparent's stud.

sentences.zh: 後同楊諒反，誅。

translations.literal: Later he joined Yang Liang's rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Yang Liang's rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: ○趙芬

translations.literal: ○ Zhao Fen
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhao Fen

sentences.zh: 趙芬，字士茂，天水西人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Fen, style name Shimao, was a man of Western Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Fen, whose style name was Shimao, came from Western Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 父演，周秦州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Governor of Qin Province under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been Governor of Qin Province under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 芬少有辯智，頗涉經史。

translations.literal: Fen in youth had eloquence and wisdom and had dipped considerably into the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Fen was quick-witted from youth and well read in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 周太祖引為相府鎧曹參軍，曆記室，累遷熊州刺史。

translations.literal: The Zhou Founder drew him in as Staff Officer of the Armourer's Office in the Chancellor's Office, passed through the secretariat, and was transferred in succession to Governor of Xiong Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Founder appointed him to the chancellor's armoury staff, then the secretariat, and eventually governor of Xiong Province.

sentences.zh: 撫納降附，得二千戶，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He pacified and accepted those who surrendered, obtaining two thousand households, and was given Opening the Office with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: By winning over surrendered populations he added two thousand households to the rolls and was granted third-rank honors with full ceremonial equipage.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護召為中外府掾，俄遷吏部下大夫。

translations.literal: The Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu summoned him as clerk of the Inner and Outer Office, and soon he was moved to Grand Master of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu brought him into the inner and outer chancellery staff, and he soon became a senior officer in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 芬性強濟，所居之職，皆有聲績。

translations.literal: Fen by nature was forceful and capable; in every post he held there were reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Fen was forceful and capable, and in every post he left a record of distinction.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，拜內史下大夫，轉少禦正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Fen was appointed Junior Grand Master of the Imperial Secretariat and transferred to Junior Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took personal control of government, Fen was made a junior grand master of the Secretariat and then junior director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 芬明習故事，每朝廷有所疑議，眾不能決者，芬輒為評斷，莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Fen was clear and practiced in precedent; whenever the court had doubtful points on which the multitude could not decide, Fen would judge and decide, and none failed to praise it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Fen knew precedent inside out; whenever the court deadlocked on a doubtful point, his ruling won universal praise.

sentences.zh: 後為司會，申國公李穆之討齊也，引為行軍長史，封淮安縣男，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Later he was Director of Accounts; when Duke Li Mu of Shen campaigned against Qi, he was drawn in as campaign chief clerk, enfeoffed as Baron of Huai'an County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He later became director of accounts; when Duke Li Mu of Shen marched against Qi, Fen served as his campaign chief clerk and was enfeoffed as Baron of Huai'an with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 複出為淅州刺史，轉東京小宗伯，鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: He again went out as Governor of Xi Province, was transferred to Junior Minister of the Imperial Clan for the Eastern Capital, and garrisoned Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was again sent out as governor of Xi Province, then made junior minister of the imperial clan for the eastern capital and stationed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥與司馬消難陰謀往來，芬察知之，密白高祖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, Yuwen Jiong and Sima Xiaonan had secret plots going back and forth; Fen detected this and secretly reported to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was still chancellor, Fen detected secret collusion between Yuwen Jiong and Sima Xiaonan and reported it confidentially.

sentences.zh: 由是深見親委，遷東京左僕射，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: Because of this he was deeply trusted and entrusted, was moved to Left Vice Director of the Eastern Capital, and advanced in rank to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby won deep trust, was made Left Vice Director of the eastern capital, and advanced to commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，罷東京官，拜尚書左僕射，與郢國公王誼修律令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang the Eastern Capital offices were abolished; he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and, with Duke Wang Yi of Ying, revised the statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang the eastern capital administration was abolished; he became Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and joined Duke Wang Yi of Ying in revising the code.

sentences.zh: 俄兼內史令，上甚信任之。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Director of the Secretariat; the Emperor greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also served as director of the Secretariat, in which post the emperor placed great confidence.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以老病出拜蒲州刺史，加金紫光祿大夫，仍領關東運漕，賜錢百萬、粟五千石而遣之。

translations.literal: Before long, for old age and illness he went out as Governor of Pu Province, was given the additional title of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, still oversaw transport and grain shipment east of the Pass, and was sent off with a gift of one million cash and five thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, citing age and illness, he was sent out as governor of Pu with the honorific title of grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon, while still overseeing grain transport east of the Pass; he was dismissed with one million cash and five thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 後數年，上表乞骸骨，征還京師，賜以二馬軺車，幾杖被褥，歸於家，皇太子又致巾帔。

translations.literal: Several years later he submitted a memorial begging to surrender his bones, was summoned back to the capital, was granted a two-horse light carriage, a staff, bedding, and quilt, and returned home; the Crown Prince also sent headcloth and scarf.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he asked to retire; recalled to the capital, he was given a two-horse carriage, staff, bedding, and quilt for his home, and the crown prince sent headcloth and scarf as well.

sentences.zh: 後數年，卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 上遣使致祭，鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to perform the sacrifice, and the Court of Diplomatic Reception supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to offer sacrifices, and the Court of Diplomatic Reception oversaw the funeral.

sentences.zh: 子元恪嗣，官至揚州總管司馬，左遷候衛長史。

translations.literal: His son Yuankuo succeeded him and reached the office of Military Affairs Officer of the Yangzhou Grand Commandery, then was demoted to Chief Clerk of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuankuo succeeded him, rose to military affairs officer of the Yangzhou commandery, and was later demoted to chief clerk of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 少子元楷，與元恪皆明幹世事。

translations.literal: The younger son Yuankai, with Yuankuo, were both clear and capable in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Yuankai, like Yuankuo, was sharp and capable in public affairs.

sentences.zh: 元楷大業中為曆陽郡丞，與廬江郡丞徐仲宗皆竭百姓之產以貢於帝。

translations.literal: In the Daye era Yuankai was Assistant Governor of Liyang Commandery; he and the Assistant Governor of Lujiang Commandery, Xu Zhongzong, both exhausted the people's wealth to present tribute to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daye, Yuankai was assistant governor of Liyang; he and Xu Zhongzong, assistant governor of Lujiang, both drained the people to furnish tribute for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 仲宗遷南郡丞，元楷超拜江都郡丞，兼領江都宮使。

translations.literal: Zhongzong was moved to Assistant Governor of Nan Commandery; Yuankai was promoted by special order to Assistant Governor of Jiangdu Commandery and additionally oversaw the Jiangdu palace mission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong was transferred to Nan commandery; Yuankai was promoted out of turn to Jiangdu and also placed in charge of the Jiangdu palace.

sentences.zh: ○楊尚希

translations.literal: ○ Yang Shangxi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yang Shangxi

sentences.zh: 楊尚希，弘農人也。

translations.literal: Yang Shangxi was a man of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shangxi came from Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 祖真，魏天水太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Tianshui in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen had been Administrator of Tianshui under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父承賓，商、直、淅三州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chengbin was Governor of the three provinces Shang, Zhi, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengbin had governed the three provinces of Shang, Zhi, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 尚希齠齔而孤。

translations.literal: Shangxi lost his father while still in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi was orphaned in early childhood.

sentences.zh: 年十一，辭母請受業長安。

translations.literal: At age eleven he took leave of his mother and requested to pursue studies in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he asked his mother's leave to study in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 涿郡盧辯見而異之，令入太學，專精不倦，同輩皆共推伏。

translations.literal: Lu Bian of Zhuo Commandery saw him and found him extraordinary, had him enter the Imperial Academy, studied with single-minded diligence without weariness, and his peers all together deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Bian of Zhuo Commandery was struck by the boy and enrolled him in the Imperial Academy; he studied with tireless focus, and his classmates all looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 周太祖嘗親臨釋奠，尚希時年十八，令講《孝經》，詞旨可觀。

translations.literal: The Zhou Founder once personally attended the libation ceremony; Shangxi was then eighteen, was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and his words and purport were admirable.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou Founder attended the ceremonial libation in person, the eighteen-year-old Shangxi was asked to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety and acquitted himself admirably.

sentences.zh: 太祖奇之，賜姓普六茹氏，擢為國子博士。

translations.literal: The Founder found him extraordinary, granted the surname Puliuru, and promoted him to Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder was impressed, granted him the surname Puliuru, and made him an erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 累轉舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 仕明、武世，曆太學博士、太子宮尹、計部中大夫，賜爵高都縣侯，東京司憲中大夫。

translations.literal: Serving through the Ming and Wu reigns, he passed through Erudite of the Imperial University, Director of the Heir Apparent's Palace, Grand Master of the Accounting Bureau, was granted the title Marquis of Gaodu County, and Eastern Capital Grand Master of the Bureau of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming and Wu emperors he served as academy erudite, director of the heir apparent's palace, senior officer of the accounting bureau, was made Marquis of Gaodu, and held a senior post in the eastern capital judiciary.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，令尚希撫慰山東、河北，至相州而帝崩，與相州總管尉迥發喪於館。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he ordered Shangxi to comfort Shandong and Hebei; he reached Xiang Province when the Emperor died, and with the Xiangzhou Grand Commander Yuwen Jiong announced the mourning at the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan sent him to reassure Shandong and Hebei; he reached Xiang Province just as the emperor died, and with the Xiangzhou commander Yuwen Jiong announced the mourning at their quarters.

sentences.zh: 尚希出謂左右曰：「蜀公哭不哀而視不安，將有他計。

translations.literal: Shangxi went out and said to those at his side, "The Duke of Shu weeps without grief and his gaze is uneasy—he will have another plan.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi stepped outside and told his attendants, "The Duke of Shu is not grieving as he should, and his eyes are restless—he is plotting something.

sentences.zh: 吾不去，將及於難。」

translations.literal: If I do not leave, I will meet with calamity."
translations.idiomatic: If I stay, I will be caught up in disaster.

sentences.zh: 遂夜中從捷徑而遁。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the middle of the night he fled by a swift bypath.
translations.idiomatic: That night he escaped by a back road.

sentences.zh: 遲明，迥方覺，分數十騎自驛路追之，不及，遂歸京師。

translations.literal: At dawn Jiong only then noticed; he divided several tens of horsemen to pursue along the post road but did not overtake him, and Shangxi thereupon returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Jiong realized he was gone and sent dozens of horsemen down the post road in pursuit, but could not catch him; Shangxi reached the capital safely.

sentences.zh: 高祖以尚希宗室之望，又背迥而至，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Shangxi had the prestige of the imperial clan and had turned his back on Jiong to come, treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu treated him with great favor, both for his standing among the imperial clan and for having abandoned Jiong to come to him.

sentences.zh: 及迥屯兵武陟，遣尚希督宗室兵三千人鎮潼關。

translations.literal: When Jiong stationed troops at Wuzhi, he sent Shangxi to oversee three thousand imperial-clan troops garrisoning Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong massed troops at Wuzhi, Shangxi was sent to hold Tong Pass with three thousand clan troops.

sentences.zh: 尋授司會中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master of the Bureau of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made senior officer of the Bureau of Accounts.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜度支尚書，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Shangxi was appointed Director of the Department of Revenue and advanced in rank to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed Director of the Department of Revenue and advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出為河南道行台兵部尚書，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: After more than a year he went out as Director of the Department of War for the Henan Circuit Mobile Commandery, with the additional title of Grand Master with Silver Seal and Green Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made Director of the Department of War on the Henan circuit staff, with the honorific rank of grand master of the silver seal and green ribbon.

sentences.zh: 尚希時見天下州郡過多，上表曰：「自秦並天下，罷侯置守，漢、魏及晉，邦邑屢改。

translations.literal: Shangxi at that time saw that prefectures and commanderies throughout the realm were too many, and submitted a memorial, saying, "Since Qin united the realm, abolished the feudal lords and set up administrators, through Han, Wei, and Jin the states and towns were repeatedly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi observed that the empire had too many prefectures and submitted a memorial: "Since Qin united the realm and replaced feudal lords with administrators, Han, Wei, and Jin repeatedly reorganized their administrative divisions.

sentences.zh: 竊見當今郡縣，倍多於古，或地無百里，數縣並置，或戶不滿千，二郡分領。

translations.literal: I observe that today's commanderies and counties are more than double those of antiquity: some lands are less than a hundred li yet several counties are set up together, or households do not reach a thousand yet two commanderies divide jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Today there are more than twice as many districts as in antiquity—some cover less than a hundred li yet host several counties, others have fewer than a thousand households yet are split between two commanderies.

sentences.zh: 具僚以眾，資費日多；

translations.literal: Staff officers are numerous, and expenses daily increase;
translations.idiomatic: Staff multiply and costs rise daily;

sentences.zh: 吏卒人倍，租調歲減。

translations.literal: clerks and soldiers double in number, and land tax and corvée decrease year by year.
translations.idiomatic: clerks and soldiers double while land tax and corvée shrink each year.

sentences.zh: 清幹良才，百分無一，動須數萬，如何可覓？

translations.literal: Clear and capable fine talent, not one in a hundred—yet several tens of thousands are needed at a stroke; how can they be found?
translations.idiomatic: Not one capable man in a hundred, yet tens of thousands of posts must be filled—where are such men to be found?

sentences.zh: 所謂民少官多，十羊九牧。

translations.literal: This is what is called few people and many officials—ten sheep and nine herdsmen.
translations.idiomatic: This is the proverb of few people and many officials—ten sheep with nine shepherds.

sentences.zh: 琴有更張之義，瑟無膠柱之理。

translations.literal: The zither has the principle of restringing; the se has no logic of gluing the bridges.
translations.idiomatic: A zither must be restrung when needed; a se cannot be played with glued bridges.

sentences.zh: 今存要去閑，並小為大，國家則不虧粟帛，選舉則易得賢才，敢陳管見，伏聽裁處。」

translations.literal: Now keep what is essential, remove what is idle, merge small into large—the state will not lose grain and silk, and in selection fine talent will be easily obtained. I dare present this narrow view and bow to hear your decision."
translations.idiomatic: Keep what is essential, cut the redundant, merge small units into large ones—the treasury will not suffer, and worthy men will be easier to find. I submit this humble view for your judgment.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而嘉之，於是遂罷天下諸郡。

translations.literal: The Emperor read it and commended it, and thereupon abolished all commanderies throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with approval and abolished commanderies empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 尋拜瀛州刺史，未之官，奉詔巡省淮南。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Ying Province, did not take up the post, and received an edict to tour and inspect Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Ying but never took up the post, receiving instead an edict to inspect Huainan.

sentences.zh: 還除兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Director of the Department of War.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Director of the Department of War.

sentences.zh: 俄轉禮部尚書，授上儀同。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to Director of the Department of Rites and granted Senior Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Director of the Department of Rites and was granted senior equipage.

sentences.zh: 尚希性弘厚，兼以學業自通，甚有雅望，為朝廷所重。

translations.literal: Shangxi by nature was broad and generous, and through scholarship made himself accomplished; he had great refined reputation and was valued by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi was magnanimous by nature and accomplished through learning; he enjoyed high esteem and the court held him in great regard.

sentences.zh: 上時每旦臨朝，日側不倦，尚希諫曰：「周文王以憂勤損壽，武王以安樂延年。

translations.literal: The Emperor at that time each dawn attended court and at sunset was not weary; Shangxi remonstrated, saying, "King Wen of Zhou through worry and diligence shortened his years; King Wu through peace and joy extended his years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held court each dawn and worked until sunset without rest; Shangxi advised him: "King Wen of Zhou shortened his life through overwork; King Wu of Zhou lived long through ease.

sentences.zh: 願陛下舉大綱，責成宰輔，繁碎之務，非人主所宜親也。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to grasp the great outline, charge the chancellor and aides with fulfillment, for trivial and fragmented affairs are not what the sovereign should personally attend to."
translations.idiomatic: Take hold of the great principles, hold your ministers accountable, and leave petty matters to them—the ruler should not attend to every detail.

sentences.zh: 上歡然曰：「公愛我者。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said with pleasure, "You are one who loves Us."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said warmly, "You care for me.

sentences.zh: 尚希素有足疾，上謂之曰：「蒲州出美酒，足堪養病，屈公臥治之。」

translations.literal: Shangxi had long had foot ailment; the Emperor said to him, "Pu Province produces fine wine, quite sufficient to nourish illness—We beg you to govern from bed."
translations.idiomatic: Shangxi had long suffered from foot trouble; the emperor told him, "Pu Province has fine wine for your ailment—go there and govern from your bed.

sentences.zh: 於是出拜蒲州刺史，仍領本州宗團驃騎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went out as Governor of Pu Province and still oversaw the clan regiment cavalry of that province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Pu while retaining command of the provincial clan cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尚希在州，甚有惠政，複引瀵水，立堤防，開稻田數千頃，民賴其利。

translations.literal: Shangxi in the province had very benevolent administration; he again led the Fen River, set up dikes and barriers, opened several thousand qing of paddy fields, and the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: In Pu he governed with great benevolence, diverted the Fen River, built dikes, and opened several thousand qing of paddy fields on which the people depended.

sentences.zh: 開皇十年卒官，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kaihuang he died in office, at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the tenth year of Kaihuang, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 諡曰平。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Ping.

sentences.zh: 子旻嗣，後改封丹水縣公，官至安定郡丞。

translations.literal: His son Min succeeded him, later had his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Danshui County, and reached the office of Assistant Governor of Anding Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min succeeded him, was later re-enfeoffed as Duke of Danshui, and rose to assistant governor of Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: ○長孫平

translations.literal: ○ Zhangsun Ping
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhangsun Ping

sentences.zh: 開皇三年，征拜度支尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaihuang he was summoned and appointed Director of the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaihuang he was recalled and appointed Director of the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 平見天下州縣多罹水旱，百姓不給，奏令民間每秋家出粟麥一石已下，貧富差等，儲之閭巷，以備凶年，各曰義倉。

translations.literal: Ping saw that prefectures and counties throughout the realm suffered much from flood and drought and the people lacked provision; he memorialized ordering that each autumn every household contribute grain or wheat of one picul or less, with gradations by rich and poor, stored in lanes and alleys against famine years, each called a Charity Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing widespread flood and drought leave the people destitute, Ping proposed that each autumn every household contribute up to one picul of grain or wheat according to means, stored in neighborhood granaries against famine—the charity granary system.

sentences.zh: 因上書曰：「臣聞國以民為本，民以食為命，勸農重谷，先王令軌。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that the state takes the people as foundation, the people take food as life, and encouraging agriculture and valuing grain are the statutes of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote further: "The state rests on the people, the people on food—encouraging agriculture and valuing grain were the laws of the sage kings.

sentences.zh: 古者三年耕而餘一年之積，九年作而有三年之儲，雖水旱為災，而民無菜色，皆由勸導有方，蓄積先備者也。

translations.literal: In antiquity three years of plowing left one year's surplus, nine years of labor left three years' stores; though flood and drought were calamities, the people had no pallor—all because guidance was well directed and stores were prepared in advance.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity three years' farming yielded one year's surplus and nine years' labor three years' stores; even in flood or drought the people did not go hungry, because guidance was sound and reserves were laid up in advance.

sentences.zh: 去年亢陽，關右饑餒，陛下運山東之粟，置常平之官，開發倉廩，普加賑賜，大德鴻恩，可謂至矣。

translations.literal: Last year there was severe drought; west of the Pass there was famine; Your Majesty transported grain from east of the mountains, set up Ever-Normal officials, opened granaries, and broadly bestowed relief—great virtue and vast grace can be called utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's drought brought famine west of the Pass; Your Majesty shipped grain from the east, established ever-normal granaries, opened the storehouses, and gave relief on a grand scale—mercy could go no further.

sentences.zh: 然經國之道，義資遠算，請勒諸州刺史、縣令，以勸農積穀為務。

translations.literal: Yet the way of governing the state rightly relies on far-reaching calculation; I ask to instruct all prefectural governors and county magistrates to make encouraging agriculture and storing grain their task.
translations.idiomatic: Yet sound governance requires foresight—I urge that all governors and magistrates make encouraging farming and storing grain their chief duty.

sentences.zh: 「上深嘉納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor deeply commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor warmly approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 自是州裡豐衍，民多賴焉。

translations.literal: From this the districts were abundant and the people largely relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Districts thereafter grew prosperous and the people benefited greatly.

sentences.zh: 後數載，轉工部尚書，名為稱職。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Director of the Department of Works and was known as fulfilling his office.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he became Director of the Department of Works and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 時有人告大都督邴紹非毀朝廷為憒憒者，上怒，將斬之。

translations.literal: At that time someone reported that Grand Commander Bing Shao had slandered the court as muddled; the Emperor was angry and was about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that Grand Commander Bing Shao had called the court muddled and incompetent, the emperor flew into a rage and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 平進諫曰：「川澤納汙，所以成其深；

translations.literal: Ping advanced and remonstrated, saying, "Rivers and marshes receive filth, thereby achieving their depth;
translations.idiomatic: Ping remonstrated: "Rivers and marshes accept filth and thereby grow deep;

sentences.zh: 山嶽藏疾，所以就其大。

translations.literal: mountains and peaks harbor sickness, thereby achieving their greatness.
translations.idiomatic: mountains harbor flaws and thereby attain their height.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝至願，願陛下弘山海之量，茂寬裕之德。

translations.literal: Your servant cannot overcome his utmost wish: I wish Your Majesty to expand the measure of mountains and seas and flourish the virtue of generosity.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to embrace the breadth of mountains and seas and cultivate a generous spirit.

sentences.zh: 鄙諺曰：'不癡不聾，未堪作大家翁。

translations.literal: A rustic saying goes, 'Without some deafness and foolishness, one cannot serve as head of the great household.
translations.idiomatic: A common saying runs, 'Without a touch of deafness and foolishness, one cannot be master of a great household.

sentences.zh: '此言雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: Though this saying is small, it can illustrate what is great.
translations.idiomatic: Small as the saying is, it applies to great matters.

sentences.zh: 邴紹之言，不應聞奏，陛下又複誅之，臣恐百代之後，有虧聖德。」

translations.literal: Xing Shao's words should not have been reported to the throne; Your Majesty again executes him—your servant fears that a hundred generations hence there will be impairment of sagely virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao's words should never have reached Your Majesty; to execute him now may stain Your sagely virtue for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 上於是赦紹。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon pardoned Shao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon pardoned Shao.

sentences.zh: 因敕群臣，誹謗之罪，勿複以聞。

translations.literal: He then instructed the ministers that crimes of slander should no longer be reported.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered that slander cases were no longer to be reported to him.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥達頭可汗與都藍可汗相攻，各遣使請授。

translations.literal: Afterward the Türk khagans Datou and Duluo attacked each other, each sending envoys to request investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Türk khagans Datou and Duluo fought each other, each sending envoys to seek imperial support.

sentences.zh: 上使平持節宣諭，令其和解，賜縑三百匹，良馬一匹而遣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Ping bearing credentials to proclaim and instruct, ordering them to reconcile, granted three hundred bolts of silk and one fine horse, and dispatched him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Ping with imperial credentials to urge reconciliation, gave him three hundred bolts of silk and a fine horse, and dispatched him.

sentences.zh: 平至突厥所，為陳利害，遂各解兵。

translations.literal: Ping reached the Türk camp, set forth advantage and harm, and they each disbanded their troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the Türk camp Ping explained the stakes, and both sides disbanded their armies.

sentences.zh: 可汗贈平馬二百匹。

translations.literal: The khagan presented Ping two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: The khagan gave him two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 及還，平進所得馬，上盡以賜之。

translations.literal: On return Ping presented the horses obtained; the Emperor bestowed them all back on him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Ping presented the horses; the emperor gave them all back to him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遇譴，以尚書檢校汴州事。

translations.literal: Before long he met with reprimand and, as Director, inspected affairs of Bian Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was reprimanded and sent to oversee Bian Province in his capacity as director.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，除汴州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Governor of Bian Province.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was appointed governor of Bian Province.

sentences.zh: 其後曆許、貝二州，俱有善政。

translations.literal: Afterward he passed through the two provinces Xu and Bei, both with good administration.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Xu and Bei provinces, both with distinction.

sentences.zh: 鄴都俗薄，舊號難治，前後刺史多不稱職。

translations.literal: The customs of the Ye capital were shallow; it was of old called hard to govern, and governors before and after mostly did not fulfill their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Ye had a reputation for lax morals and was hard to govern; few of its governors had succeeded.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以平所在善稱，轉相州刺史。

translations.literal: The court, because Ping wherever he was had a reputation for goodness, transferred him to Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The court transferred him to Xiang Province on his record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 甚有能名。

translations.literal: He had a great reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He earned a strong reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 在州數年，會正月十五日，百姓大戲，畫衣裳為鍪甲之象，上怒而免之。

translations.literal: Several years in the province, it happened on the fifteenth day of the first month that the people held great revels and painted garments in the likeness of helmets and armor; the Emperor was angry and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office, on the Lantern Festival the people staged revels painting their clothes to resemble armor; the emperor was angered and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 俄而念平鎮淮南時事，進位大將軍，拜太常卿，判吏部尚書事。

translations.literal: Shortly the Emperor recalled Ping's service when he garrisoned Huainan, advanced him to Grand General, appointed him Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and had him decide affairs of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon remembering his service in Huainan, the emperor promoted him to grand general, made him Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and put him in charge of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中卒官。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office during the Renshou era.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Kang.

sentences.zh: 子師孝，性輕狡好利，數犯法。

translations.literal: His son Shixiao by nature was frivolous, cunning, and fond of profit, and repeatedly violated the law.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixiao was frivolous, cunning, and greedy, and repeatedly broke the law.

sentences.zh: 上以其不克負荷，遣使吊平國官。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because he could not bear the burden, sent envoys to offer condolences at Ping's state funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, deeming the son unworthy of his father's legacy, sent envoys to condole at Ping's funeral.

sentences.zh: 師孝後為渤海郡主簿，屬大業之季，政教陵遲，師孝恣行貪濁，一郡苦之。

translations.literal: Shixiao later was Chief Clerk of Bohai Commandery; in the late Daye era government and teaching declined, and Shixiao wantonly practiced greed and corruption—the whole commandery suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiao later served as chief clerk of Bohai; in the late Daye era, as governance collapsed, he plundered the commandery without restraint.

sentences.zh: 後為王世充所害。

translations.literal: Later he was harmed by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later killed by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: ○元軍

translations.literal: ○ Yuan Hui
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yuan Hui

sentences.zh: 元暉，字叔平，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Hui, style name Shuping, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hui, whose style name was Shuping, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖琛，魏恆、朔二州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chen was Governor of the two provinces Heng and Shuo in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chen had governed Heng and Shuo provinces under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父翌，尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi had been Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 暉鬚眉如畫，進止可觀，頗好學，涉獵書記。

translations.literal: Hui's beard and brows were as if painted, his comings and goings admirable; he was quite fond of learning and ranged through books and records.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had finely drawn brows and beard and graceful bearing; he loved learning and read widely in books and records.

sentences.zh: 少得美名於京下，周太祖見而禮之，命與諸子遊處，每同席共硯，情契甚厚。

translations.literal: In youth he gained a fine reputation in the capital; the Zhou Founder saw him and treated him with ceremony, ordered him to roam and dwell with his sons, each time sharing mat and inkstone—the bond of feeling was very thick.
translations.idiomatic: He won an early reputation in the capital; the Zhou Founder honored him and had him study with his sons, sharing desk and inkstone in close friendship.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，召補相府中兵參軍，尋遷武伯下大夫。

translations.literal: At capped age he was summoned to fill the post of Middle Troops Staff Officer in the Chancellor's Office, and soon was moved to Junior Grand Master of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping ceremony he was appointed middle troops staff officer in the chancellor's office and soon promoted to junior grand master of the martial guard.

sentences.zh: 于時突厥屢為寇患，朝廷將結和親，令暉齎錦彩十萬，使於突厥。

translations.literal: At that time the Türks repeatedly made incursions; the court was about to conclude a marriage alliance and ordered Hui to carry one hundred thousand worth of brocades and silks as envoy to the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: As the Türks raided repeatedly, the court prepared a marriage alliance and sent Hui with brocades and silks worth one hundred thousand to the Türk court.

sentences.zh: 暉說以利害，申國厚禮，可汗大悅，遣其名王隨獻方物。

translations.literal: Hui explained advantage and harm and declared the state's generous gifts; the khagan was greatly pleased and sent his titled kings to follow with presentation of local products.
translations.idiomatic: Hui explained the stakes and presented the court's generous gifts; the khagan was delighted and sent his nobles with tribute.

sentences.zh: 俄拜儀同三司、賓部下大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Third Rank with Equipage and Grand Master of the Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a third-rank general and senior officer of the guests bureau.

sentences.zh: 保定初，大塚宰宇文護引為長史，會齊人來結盟好，以暉多才辯，與千乘公崔睦俱使于齊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding the Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu drew him in as Chief Clerk; it happened that the Qi came to form a league of friendship, and because Hui had much talent and eloquence, he was sent to Qi together with Duke Cui Mu of Qiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoding, Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu made him chief clerk; when Qi sought an alliance, Hui's eloquence won him appointment as envoy to Qi with Duke Cui Mu of Qiansheng.

sentences.zh: 遷振威中大夫。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Master Who Shakes Might.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master who shakes might.

sentences.zh: 武帝之娉突厥後也，令暉致禮焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu betrothed a Türk princess, he ordered Hui to convey the ceremonial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu betrothed a Türk princess, Hui was sent to deliver the betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 加開府，轉司憲大夫。

translations.literal: He was given Opening the Office and transferred to Grand Master of the Bureau of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted opening the office and made grand master of the Bureau of Justice.

sentences.zh: 及平關東，使暉安集河北，封義寧子，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: When the east of the Pass was pacified, Hui was sent to settle and gather Hebei, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yining with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of the east, he was sent to stabilize Hebei and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yining with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 高祖總百揆，加上開府，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu oversaw all affairs, he was given the additional title of Opening the Office and advanced in rank to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took charge of government, Hui was given opening the office and advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜都官尚書，兼領太僕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Justice and additionally oversaw the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he became Director of the Bureau of Justice while also overseeing the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 奏請決杜陽水灌三畤原，溉舄鹵之地數千頃，民賴其利。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to breach the Duyang River to irrigate the Sanchi plain, watering several thousand qing of brackish land, and the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed diverting the Duyang River to irrigate the Sanchi plain, reclaiming several thousand qing of saline land for the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉左武候將軍，太僕卿如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to General of the Left Martial Guard and remained Director of the Imperial Stud as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became general of the left martial guard while retaining the directorship of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 尋轉兵部尚書，監漕渠之役。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Department of War and oversaw the canal transport labor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Director of the Department of War and supervised work on the transport canals.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐事免。

translations.literal: Before long, for an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 頃之，拜魏州刺史，頗有惠政。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Governor of Wei Province and had quite benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed governor of Wei Province and governed with notable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 在任數年，以疾去職。

translations.literal: Several years in office, he left his post because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒于京師，時年六十。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died in the capital, at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the capital a year later, at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 上嗟悼久之，敕鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed in lament for a long while and ordered the Court of Diplomatic Reception to supervise the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him at length and ordered the Court of Diplomatic Reception to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 諡曰元。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子肅嗣，官至光祿少卿。

translations.literal: His son Su succeeded him and reached the office of Vice Director of the Court for Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su succeeded him and rose to vice director of the Court for Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 肅弟仁器，性明敏，官至日南郡丞。

translations.literal: Su's younger brother Renqi by nature was clear and keen and reached the office of Assistant Governor of Rinan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Su's younger brother Renqi was sharp and capable and rose to assistant governor of Rinan commandery.

sentences.zh: ○韋師

translations.literal: ○ Wei Shi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wei Shi

sentences.zh: 韋師，字公穎，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Wei Shi, style name Gongying, was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shi, whose style name was Gongying, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父瑱，周驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was Grand General of Agile Cavalry under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had been Grand General of Agile Cavalry under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 師少沉謹，有至性。

translations.literal: Shi in youth was grave and careful, with utmost nature.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was grave and careful from youth, with a deeply sincere nature.

sentences.zh: 初就學，始讀《孝經》，舍書而歎曰：「名教之極，其在茲乎！」

translations.literal: When he first pursued study and began reading the Classic of Filial Piety, he set down the book and sighed, saying, "The utmost of name and teaching—is it not here!"
translations.idiomatic: When he first began his studies and read the Classic of Filial Piety, he set the book down and exclaimed, "The summit of moral teaching—is it not here!

sentences.zh: 少丁父母憂，居喪盡禮，州裡稱其孝行。

translations.literal: In youth he met his parents' bereavement, observed mourning with full rites, and the district praised his filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he observed mourning with full propriety, and the district praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 及長，略涉經史，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: When he grew up he dipped slightly into classics and histories and was especially skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he gained some learning in the classics and histories and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 周大塚宰宇文護引為中外府記室，轉賓曹參軍。

translations.literal: The Zhou Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu drew him in as Recorder of the Inner and Outer Office and transferred him to Staff Officer of the Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu appointed him recorder of the inner and outer chancellery, then staff officer of the guests bureau.

sentences.zh: 師雅知諸蕃風俗及山川險易，其有夷狄朝貢，師必接對，論其國俗，如視諸掌。

translations.literal: Shi elegantly knew the customs of the various frontier peoples and the ease or peril of mountains and rivers; whenever barbarians came to court with tribute, Shi always received and answered them, discussing their national customs as if viewing them on his palm.
translations.idiomatic: Shi knew the customs of the frontier peoples and the terrain they crossed; whenever tribes came to pay tribute, he received them and discussed their lands as if he held them in his palm.

sentences.zh: 夷人驚服，無敢隱情。

translations.literal: The barbarians were startled into submission and did not dare conceal facts.
translations.idiomatic: They were astonished into candor and dared hide nothing from him.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲為雍州牧，引為主簿，本官如故。

translations.literal: Prince Xian of Qi was Governor of Yong Province and drew him in as Chief Clerk, his original office as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xian of Qi became governor of Yong Province, he made Shi his chief clerk while retaining his original post.

sentences.zh: 及武帝親總萬機，轉少府大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Shi was transferred to Grand Master of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took personal control of government, Shi became grand master of the palace treasury.

sentences.zh: 及平高氏，詔師安撫山東，徙為賓部大夫。

translations.literal: When the Gao clan was pacified, an edict ordered Shi to pacify Shandong, and he was moved to Grand Master of the Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification of the Gao clan, he was ordered to reassure Shandong and was made grand master of the guests bureau.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜使部侍郎，賜爵井陘侯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Shi was appointed Vice Director of the Department of Envoys, granted the title Marquis of Jingxing with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed vice director of the Department of Envoys and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingxing with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 數年，遷河北道行台兵部尚書，詔為山東河南十八州安撫大使。

translations.literal: Several years later he was moved to Director of the Department of War for the Hebei Circuit Mobile Commandery and was edicted as Pacification Commissioner for the eighteen provinces of Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he became director of the Department of War on the Hebei circuit staff and was made pacification commissioner for eighteen provinces in Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 奏事稱旨，賜錢三百萬，兼領晉王廣司馬。

translations.literal: His memorials pleased the throne; he was granted three million cash and additionally oversaw the military affairs officer post of Prince Guang of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His reports pleased the emperor, who gave him three million cash and additionally made him military affairs officer to Prince Guang of Jin.

sentences.zh: 其族人世康，為吏部尚書，與師素懷勝負。

translations.literal: His clansman Shikang was Director of the Department of State Personnel and with Shi had long harbored rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Shikang, Director of the Department of State Personnel, had long been his rival.

sentences.zh: 于時晉王為雍州牧，盛存望第，以司空楊雄、尚書左僕射高熲並為州都督，引師為主簿。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Jin was Governor of Yong Province and maintained a splendid residence; the Minister of Works Yang Xiong and Left Vice Director Gao Jiong were both made provincial commanders, and Shi was drawn in as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin was governor of Yong and kept a grand residence, Minister of Works Yang Xiong and Left Vice Director Gao Jiong were made provincial commanders and Shi was appointed chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 而世康弟世約為法曹從事。

translations.literal: Yet Shikang's younger brother Shiyue was an attendant in the law bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Shikang's younger brother Shiyue served as an attendant in the law bureau.

sentences.zh: 世康恚恨不能食，又恥世約在師之下，召世約數之曰：「汝何故為從事？」

translations.literal: Shikang was resentful and could not eat, and was ashamed that Shiyue ranked below Shi; he summoned Shiyue and reproached him, saying, "Why do you serve as attendant?"
translations.idiomatic: Shikang was so furious he could not eat, shamed that Shiyue ranked below Shi; he summoned his brother and demanded, "Why are you serving as a mere attendant?

sentences.zh: 遂杖之。

translations.literal: He thereupon beat him with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Then he had him beaten with a staff.

sentences.zh: 後從上幸醴泉宮，上召師與左僕射高熲、上柱國韓擒等，於臥內賜宴，令各敘舊事，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor on a visit to the Liquan Palace; the Emperor summoned Shi together with Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Pillar of State Han Qin, and others, bestowed a feast in the inner chamber, and ordered each to recount old affairs for laughter and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Later, accompanying the emperor to the Liquan Palace, Shi was summoned with Gao Jiong and Han Qin to a private feast where each told old stories for amusement.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以本官領元帥掾，陳國府藏，悉委于師，秋毫無所犯，稱為清白。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen he held his original office and led the marshal's staff; the Chen state's treasury stores were all entrusted to Shi, and he did not violate the slightest thing—he was called incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he served on the marshal's staff; the entire Chen treasury was placed in his charge, and he touched nothing—he was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 後上為長寧王儼納其女為妃。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor took Shi's daughter as consort for Prince Yan of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor later took his daughter as consort for Prince Yan of Changning.

sentences.zh: 除汴州刺史，甚有治名，卒官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Bian Province, had a great reputation for governance, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed governor of Bian Province, he earned a strong reputation for governance and died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Ding.

sentences.zh: 子德政嗣，大業中，仕至給事郎。

translations.literal: His son Dezheng succeeded him; in the Daye era he served up to Attendant Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dezheng succeeded him and under Daye rose to attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: ○楊異

translations.literal: ○ Yang Yi
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yang Yi

sentences.zh: 楊異，字文殊，弘農華陰人也。

translations.literal: Yang Yi, style name Wenshu, was a man of Huayin in Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yi, whose style name was Wenshu, came from Huayin in Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 祖鈞，魏司空。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun was Minister of Works in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun had been Minister of Works under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父儉，侍中。

translations.literal: His father Jian was Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had been palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 異美風儀，沉深有器局。

translations.literal: Yi had fine bearing and presence, was deep and reserved with capacity and vision.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was handsome and dignified, grave and far-sighted.

sentences.zh: 髫齔就學，日誦千言，見者奇之。

translations.literal: While still in infancy he pursued study, reciting a thousand words a day; those who saw him found him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He began study in childhood and recited a thousand characters a day, to the astonishment of onlookers.

sentences.zh: 九歲丁父憂，哀毀過禮，殆將滅性。

translations.literal: At nine he met his father's bereavement, his grief and emaciation exceeding the rites, nearly extinguishing his nature.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he lost his father and mourned so excessively he nearly wasted away.

sentences.zh: 及免喪之後，絕慶吊，閉戶讀書。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, he ceased congratulations and condolences and closed his door to read books.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he declined all social calls and shut himself in to read.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，博涉書記。

translations.literal: Within several years he ranged broadly through books and records.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he had read widely in books and records.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝時，為甯都太守，甚有能名。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Min of Zhou he was Administrator of Ningdu and had a great reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Min of Zhou he was administrator of Ningdu and earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 賜爵昌樂縣子。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Viscount of Changle County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Changle.

sentences.zh: 後數以軍功，進為侯。

translations.literal: Later, repeatedly for military merit, he was advanced to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated military achievements later advanced him to marquis.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，行濟州事。

translations.literal: When Gaozu served as Chancellor, Yi administered affairs of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor, Yi administered Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，拜宗正少卿，加上開府。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Yi was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and given the additional title of Opening the Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was made vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan with the additional rank of opening the office.

sentences.zh: 蜀王秀之鎮益州也，朝廷盛選綱紀，以異方直，拜益州總管長史，賜錢二十萬、縑三百匹、馬五十匹而遣之。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiu of Shu garrisoned Yizhou, the court greatly selected rules and discipline; because Yi was upright, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Yizhou Grand Commandery, granted two hundred thousand cash, three hundred bolts of silk, and fifty horses, and dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiu of Shu was posted to Yizhou, the court sought a strict administrator; Yi was appointed chief clerk of the Yizhou commandery and sent off with two hundred thousand cash, three hundred bolts of silk, and fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 尋遷西南道行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Director of the Department of War for the Southwest Circuit Mobile Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became director of the Department of War on the southwest circuit staff.

sentences.zh: 數載，複為宗正少卿。

translations.literal: Several years later he again became Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he again became vice director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted and appointed Director of the Department of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Director of the Department of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出除吳州總管，甚有能名。

translations.literal: After more than a year he went out and was appointed Grand Commander of Wu Province, with a great reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made grand commander of Wu Province, where he again proved highly capable.

sentences.zh: 時晉王廣鎮揚州，詔令異每歲一與王相見，評論得失，規諷疑闕。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Guang of Jin garrisoned Yangzhou; an edict ordered Yi once a year to meet the prince, discuss gains and losses, and admonish on doubtful shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Guang of Jin was posted to Yangzhou, an edict required Yi to meet him once a year to review his conduct and offer corrective counsel.

sentences.zh: 數載，卒官，時年六十二。

translations.literal: Several years later he died in office, at age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office several years later, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 子虔遜。

translations.literal: His son Qianxun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Qianxun.

sentences.zh: ○蘇孝慈兄子沙羅

translations.literal: ○ Shaluo, nephew of Su Xiaoci
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shaluo, nephew of Su Xiaoci

sentences.zh: 蘇孝慈，扶風人也。

translations.literal: Su Xiaoci was a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Su Xiaoci came from Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父武周，周兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Wuzhou was Governor of Yan Province under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wuzhou had been Governor of Yan Province under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 孝慈少沉謹，有器幹，美容儀。

translations.literal: Xiaoci in youth was grave and careful, with capacity and backbone, and fine in appearance and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci was grave and capable from youth, handsome in bearing, and possessed of real administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 周初為中侍上士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was Senior Attendant of the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou he was a senior attendant of the inner service.

sentences.zh: 後拜都督，聘于齊，以奉使稱旨，遷大都督。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Commander, was sent as envoy to Qi, and because his mission pleased the intent he was moved to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made commander and sent as envoy to Qi; his mission pleased the court and he was promoted to grand commander.

sentences.zh: 其年又聘于齊，還授宣納上士。

translations.literal: That same year he was again sent as envoy to Qi; on return he was appointed Senior Envoy Receiver.
translations.idiomatic: The same year he went again to Qi and on return was made senior envoy receiver.

sentences.zh: 後從武帝伐齊，以功進位開府，賜爵文安縣公，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Wu in attacking Qi; for merit he was advanced to Opening the Office and granted the title Duke of Wen'an County with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu against Qi and for merit was granted opening the office and enfeoffed as Duke of Wen'an with fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋改封臨水縣公，增邑千二百戶，累遷工部上大夫。

translations.literal: Soon his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Linshui County with an added fief of one thousand two hundred households; he was transferred in succession to Senior Grand Master of the Department of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon re-enfeoffed as Duke of Linshui with an additional twelve hundred households and rose to senior grand master of the Department of Works.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進爵安平郡公，拜太府卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Xiaoci was advanced to Duke of Anping Commandery and appointed Director of the Grand Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, he was advanced to Duke of Anping and appointed Director of the Grand Treasury.

sentences.zh: 于時王業初基，百度伊始，征天下工匠，纖微之巧，無不畢集。

translations.literal: At that time the royal enterprise was just founded and the hundred regulations had just begun; craftsmen from throughout the realm were summoned, and the finest subtle skills were all gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: As the dynasty was being founded and institutions established anew, craftsmen from across the realm were summoned and the finest skills gathered.

sentences.zh: 孝慈總其事，世以為能。

translations.literal: Xiaoci oversaw all these matters, and the age considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci directed the work and was widely regarded as capable.

sentences.zh: 俄遷大司農，歲餘，拜兵部尚書，待遇逾密。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Minister of the Grand Granary; after more than a year he was appointed Director of the Department of War, and his treatment grew ever closer.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Minister of the Grand Granary, and a year later Director of the Department of War, with ever closer favor from the throne.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子勇頗知時政，上欲重宮官之望，多令大臣領其職。

translations.literal: At that time Crown Prince Yong was quite versed in current affairs; the Emperor wished to increase the prestige of palace offices and often had great ministers hold their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong was already versed in affairs of state; the emperor wished to enhance the prestige of palace offices and often had senior ministers hold them concurrently.

sentences.zh: 於是拜孝慈為太子右衛率，尚書如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xiaoci was appointed Right Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard, his directorship as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci was therefore made right commander of the crown prince's guard while retaining his ministry.

sentences.zh: 明年，上於陝州置常平倉，轉輸京下。

translations.literal: The next year the Emperor set up an Ever-Normal Granary at Shan Province to transport grain to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor established an ever-normal granary at Shan Province to ship grain to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以渭水多沙，流乍深乍淺，漕運者苦之，於是決謂水為渠以屬河，令孝慈督其役。

translations.literal: Because the Wei River had much sand and its flow was now deep and now shallow, those engaged in canal transport suffered; thereupon the Wei was breached to make a canal joining the Yellow River, and Xiaoci was ordered to supervise the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Wei was sandy and its depth unpredictable, transport was difficult; the Wei was therefore diverted into a canal joining the Yellow River, with Xiaoci supervising the work.

sentences.zh: 渠成，上善之。

translations.literal: When the canal was completed, the Emperor commended it.
translations.idiomatic: When the canal was finished, the emperor praised the achievement.

sentences.zh: 又領太子右庶子，轉授左衛率，仍判工部、民部二尚書，稱為幹理。

translations.literal: He additionally oversaw the Crown Prince's Right Vice Director, was transferred and appointed Left Commander of the Guard, and still decided affairs for the two directors of the Departments of Works and People—he was called capable in administration.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as the crown prince's right vice director, then left commander of the guard, while continuing to oversee the ministries of works and people—he was known for efficient administration.

sentences.zh: 數載，進位大將軍，轉工部尚書，率如故。

translations.literal: Several years later he was advanced to Grand General and transferred to Director of the Department of Works, his commandership as before.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was promoted to grand general and director of the Department of Works, retaining his guard command.

sentences.zh: 先是，以百僚供費不足，台省府寺咸置廨錢，收息取給。
