translations.literal: Previously, because the supply expenses of the hundred officials were insufficient, the departments, provinces, and courts all set up office funds and took interest for provision.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, because official salaries were insufficient, government offices had set up capital funds and lived off the interest.

sentences.zh: 孝慈以為官民爭利，非興化之道，上表請罷之，請公卿以下給職田各有差，上並嘉納焉。

translations.literal: Xiaoci considered that officials and people competing for profit was not the way of promoting transformation; he submitted a memorial requesting abolition and asking that from dukes and ministers downward official fields be granted each with gradations—the Emperor commended and accepted all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci held that such profiteering was unworthy of civilizing government and memorialized to abolish the funds and grant graded official fields to officials instead; the emperor approved both proposals.

sentences.zh: 開皇十八年，將廢太子，憚其在東宮，出為淅州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, when the crown prince was to be deposed, fearing Xiaoci's position in the Eastern Palace, the Emperor sent him out as Governor of Xi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, when the emperor planned to depose the crown prince, he feared Xiaoci's influence in the eastern palace and sent him out as governor of Xi Province.

sentences.zh: 太子以孝慈去，甚不平，形於言色。

translations.literal: The crown prince, because Xiaoci departed, was very displeased, and it showed in his words and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was openly displeased at Xiaoci's removal.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the weight in which he was regarded.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，遷洪州總管，俱有惠政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was moved to Grand Commander of Hong Province, in both places having benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Renshou he was made grand commander of Hong Province, governing with benevolence in both posts.

sentences.zh: 共後桂林山越相聚為亂，詔孝慈為行軍總管，擊平之。

translations.literal: Afterward the Shanyue of Guilin gathered and made rebellion; an edict appointed Xiaoci as campaign grand commander, and he struck and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Shanyue of Guilin rose in rebellion, Xiaoci was made campaign commander and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 其年卒官。

translations.literal: That year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office that same year.

sentences.zh: 有子會昌。

translations.literal: He had a son Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Huichang.

sentences.zh: 孝慈兄子沙羅，字子粹。

translations.literal: Xiaoci's nephew Shaluo, style name Zicui.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoci's nephew Shaluo, whose style name was Zicui.

sentences.zh: 父順，周眉州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Shun was Governor of Mei Province under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shun had been Governor of Mei Province under the Zhou.

sentences.zh: 沙羅仕周，釋褐都督。

translations.literal: Shaluo served Zhou and upon leaving the sackcloth was appointed Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Shaluo entered Zhou service as commander upon completing his studies.

sentences.zh: 後從韋孝寬破尉迥，以功授開府儀同三司，封通秦縣公。

translations.literal: Later he followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Jiong; for merit he was granted Opening the Office with Equipage Equal to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Duke of Tongqin County.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yuwen Jiong and was granted third-rank honors with full ceremonial equipage and enfeoffed as Duke of Tongqin.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，蜀王秀鎮益州，沙羅以本官從，拜資州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang Prince Xiu of Shu garrisoned Yizhou; Shaluo followed in his original office and was appointed Governor of Zi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang, when Prince Xiu of Shu was posted to Yizhou, Shaluo accompanied him and was appointed governor of Zi Province.

sentences.zh: 八年，冉尨羌作亂，攻汶山、金川二鎮，沙羅率兵擊破之，授邛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Ranmang Qiang made rebellion, attacking the two garrisons Wenshan and Jinchuan; Shaluo led troops to strike and defeat them and was appointed Governor of Qiong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Ranmang Qiang rebelled against the garrisons of Wenshan and Jinchuan; Shaluo defeated them and was made governor of Qiong Province.

sentences.zh: 後數載，檢校利州總管事。

translations.literal: Several years later he inspected affairs of the Lizhou Grand Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was placed in charge of the Lizhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 從史萬歲擊西爨，累戰有功，進位大將軍，賜物千段。

translations.literal: He followed Shi Wansui in attacking the Western Cuan, accumulated battles with achievement, was advanced to Grand General, and was granted a thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shi Wansui against the Western Cuan, distinguished himself in repeated battles, was promoted to grand general, and received a thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校益州總管長史。

translations.literal: Soon he inspected affairs as Chief Clerk of the Yizhou Grand Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon placed in charge as chief clerk of the Yizhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 會越歸人王奉舉兵作亂，沙羅從段文振討平之，賜奴婢百口。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Feng, a man of the Yue who had submitted, raised troops in rebellion; Shaluo followed Duan Wenzhen in campaigning to pacify him and was granted one hundred male and female servants.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Feng, a submitted Yue tribesman, rebelled, Shaluo followed Duan Wenzhen to suppress him and was rewarded with a hundred servants.

sentences.zh: 會蜀王秀廢，吏案奏沙羅雲：「王奉為奴所殺，秀乃詐稱左右斬之。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince Xiu of Shu was deposed; the clerks' investigation memorial reported Shaluo as saying, "Wang Feng was killed by a slave, yet Xiu falsely claimed his attendants beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiu of Shu was deposed, investigators reported that Shaluo had said, "Wang Feng was killed by a slave, yet Xiu falsely claimed his attendants executed him.

sentences.zh: 又調熟獠，令出奴婢，沙羅隱而不奏。」

translations.literal: He also levied the assimilated Liao, ordering them to furnish male and female servants, and Shaluo concealed this and did not report it."
translations.idiomatic: He also levied assimilated tribes for slaves, which Shaluo concealed and did not report.

sentences.zh: 由是除名，卒於家。

translations.literal: Because of this he was struck from the rolls and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore struck from the rolls and died at home.

sentences.zh: 有子康。

translations.literal: He had a son Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Kang.

sentences.zh: ○李雄

translations.literal: ○ Li Xiong
translations.idiomatic: ○ Li Xiong

sentences.zh: 李雄，字毗盧，趙郡高邑人也。

translations.literal: Li Xiong, style name Pilu, was a man of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong, whose style name was Pilu, came from Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖榼，魏太中大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jie was Grand Master of Palace Counsel in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jie had been grand master of palace counsel under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 父徽伯，齊陝州刺史，陷於周，雄因隨軍入長安。

translations.literal: His father Huibo was Governor of Shan Province in Qi, was captured by Zhou, and Xiong therefore followed the army into Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huibo had been governor of Shan under Qi; when captured by the Zhou, Xiong followed the army into Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 雄少慷慨，有大志。

translations.literal: Xiong in youth was generous and ardent, with great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was generous and ambitious from youth.

sentences.zh: 家世並以學業自通，雄獨習騎射。

translations.literal: His family for generations all made their way through scholarship; Xiong alone practiced mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: His family had risen through scholarship for generations; Xiong alone trained in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 其兄子旦讓之曰：「棄文尚武，非士大夫之素業。」

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Zidan remonstrated with him, saying, "Abandoning letters and honoring arms is not the constant occupation of scholar-officials."
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zidan admonished him: "To abandon learning for martial arts is not the scholar-official's proper path.

sentences.zh: 雄答曰：「竊覽自古誠臣貴仕，文武不備而能濟其功業者鮮矣。

translations.literal: Xiong answered, "I have privately surveyed that from antiquity sincere ministers and honored officials who lacked both civil and martial accomplishment yet could complete their achievements and enterprises have been few.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong replied: "I have observed that few loyal ministers and eminent officials in history achieved great things without both civil and martial competence.

sentences.zh: 雄雖不敏，頗觀前志，但不守章句耳。

translations.literal: Although Xiong is not keen, I have quite observed the records of former times—I simply do not cling to exegetical clauses.
translations.idiomatic: I am no genius, but I have read the ancients—I simply refuse to be bound by textual commentary alone.

sentences.zh: 既文且武，兄何病焉！」

translations.literal: Having both civil and martial accomplishment, elder brother, what fault do you find!"
translations.idiomatic: Being skilled in both letters and arms—what fault do you find in that!

sentences.zh: 子旦無以應之。

translations.literal: Zidan had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zidan had no reply.

sentences.zh: 周太祖時，釋褐輔國將軍。

translations.literal: In the time of the Zhou Founder, upon leaving the sackcloth he was appointed General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou Founder he entered service as general who assists the state.

sentences.zh: 從達奚武平漢中，定興州，又討汾州叛胡，錄前後功，拜驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He followed Daxi Wu in pacifying Hanzhong, settling Xing Province, and again campaigning against the rebel Hu of Fen Province; his achievements before and after were recorded, and he was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Third Rank with Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Daxi Wu in pacifying Hanzhong and Xing Province and suppressing rebels in Fen Province; for these cumulative achievements he was made grand general of agile cavalry and a third-rank general.

sentences.zh: 閔帝受禪，進爵為公，遷小賓部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min received the abdication, Xiong was advanced to Duke and moved to the Junior Guests Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min took the throne, he was advanced to duke and moved to the junior guests bureau.

sentences.zh: 其後複從達奚武與齊人戰於芒山，諸軍大敗，雄所領獨全。

translations.literal: Afterward he again followed Daxi Wu in battling the Qi at Mangshan; the armies were greatly defeated, but those Xiong led alone were preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Daxi Wu against Qi at Mangshan; though the army was routed, the troops under his command escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，從陳王純迎後於突厥，進爵奚伯，拜硤州刺史。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu he followed Prince Chun of Chen in welcoming the empress from the Türks, was advanced to Earl of Xi, and was appointed Governor of Qia Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he accompanied Prince Chun of Chen to welcome the empress from the Türks, was advanced to Earl of Xi, and appointed governor of Qia Province.

sentences.zh: 數歲，征為本府中大夫。

translations.literal: Several years later he was summoned as Grand Master of his bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled as grand master of his bureau.

sentences.zh: 尋出為涼州總管長史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Chief Clerk of the Liangzhou Grand Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as chief clerk of the Liangzhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 從滕王逌破吐谷渾于青海，以功加上儀同。

translations.literal: He followed Prince You of Teng in defeating the Tuyuhun at Qinghai; for merit he was given the additional title of Senior Equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince You of Teng in defeating the Tuyuhun at Qinghai and was granted senior equipage for his merit.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，從行軍總管韋孝寬略定淮南。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Xiong followed Campaign Grand Commander Wei Xiaokuan in securing Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Xiong followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan.

sentences.zh: 雄以輕騎數百至硤石，說下十餘城，拜豪州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiong with several hundred light horsemen reached Qiaoshi, persuaded more than ten cities to submit, and was appointed Governor of Hao Province.
translations.idiomatic: With a few hundred light cavalry he reached Qiaoshi, won over more than ten cities, and was appointed governor of Hao Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖總百揆，征為司會中大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu oversaw all affairs, Xiong was summoned as Grand Master of the Bureau of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took charge of government, he was recalled as grand master of the Bureau of Accounts.

sentences.zh: 以淮南之功，加位上開府。

translations.literal: For his achievements in Huainan he was given the additional rank of Senior Opening the Office.
translations.idiomatic: For his Huainan achievements he was granted senior opening the office.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜鴻臚卿，進爵高都郡公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he was appointed Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception, advanced to Duke of Gaodu Commandery, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was made Director of the Court of Diplomatic Reception, advanced to Duke of Gaodu, with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後數年，晉王廣出鎮并州，以雄為河北行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Several years later Prince Guang of Jin went out to garrison Bing Province, and Xiong was made Director of the Department of War for the Hebei Mobile Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, when Prince Guang of Jin was posted to Bing Province, Xiong was made director of the Department of War on the Hebei circuit staff.

sentences.zh: 上謂雄曰：「吾兒既少，更事未多，以卿兼文武才，今推誠相委，吾無北顧之憂矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Xiong, "My son is still young and has not yet seen much service; with your combined civil and martial talent I now entrust him to you in full sincerity—I have no worry looking northward."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him, "My son is young and inexperienced; with your civil and martial gifts I entrust him to you wholeheartedly—I need no longer worry about the north.

sentences.zh: 雄頓首而言曰：「陛下不以臣之不肖，寄臣以重任。

translations.literal: Xiong knocked his head and said, "Your Majesty does not regard your servant as unworthy but entrusts him with a heavy charge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty does not disdain my unworthiness but entrusts me with a grave responsibility.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚固，心非木石，謹當竭誠效命，以答鴻恩。」

translations.literal: Although your servant is foolish and obstinate, his heart is not wood or stone—I shall earnestly exhaust sincerity and offer my life to repay vast grace."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am dull and stubborn, I am not heartless—I shall serve with all my loyalty to repay your vast grace.

sentences.zh: 歔欷流涕，上慰諭而遣之。

translations.literal: He sobbed and shed tears; the Emperor comforted and instructed him and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He wept aloud; the emperor comforted him and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 雄當官正直，侃然有不可犯之色，王甚敬憚，吏民稱焉。

translations.literal: Xiong in office was upright, stern with an aspect that could not be violated; the prince greatly respected and feared him, and clerks and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In office Xiong was upright and unapproachable; the prince held him in deep respect, and officials and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒官。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office a year later.

sentences.zh: 子公挺嗣。

translations.literal: His son Gongting succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongting succeeded him.

sentences.zh: ○張煚劉仁恩郭均馮世基厙狄颭

translations.literal: ○ Zhang Jiong, Liu Ren'en, Guo Jun, Feng Shiji, and Kudiji Yan
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhang Jiong, Liu Ren'en, Guo Jun, Feng Shiji, and Kudiji Yan

sentences.zh: 張煚，字士鴻，河間鄚人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiong, style name Shihong, was a man of Mo in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiong, whose style name was Shihong, came from Mo in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 父羨，少好學，多所通涉，仕魏為蕩難將軍。

translations.literal: His father Xian in youth loved learning and ranged broadly in many fields; he served Wei as General Who Calms Difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian loved learning from youth and mastered many fields; under Wei he served as general who calms difficulty.

sentences.zh: 從武帝入關，累遷銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wu in entering the Pass and was transferred in succession to Grand Master with Silver Seal and Green Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Wu into the Pass and rose to grand master of the silver seal and green ribbon.

sentences.zh: 周太祖引為從事中郎，賜姓叱羅氏。

translations.literal: The Zhou Founder drew him in as Attendant Gentleman and granted the surname Chiluo.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Founder appointed him attendant gentleman and granted the surname Chiluo.

sentences.zh: 曆司職大夫，雍州治中、雍州刺史、儀同三司，賜爵虞鄉縣公。

translations.literal: He passed through Grand Master of the Bureau of Works, Administrator of Yong Province, Governor of Yong Province, and General of the Third Rank with Equipage, and was granted the title Duke of Yuxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand master of the bureau of works, Yongzhou administrator and governor, and third-rank general, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yuxiang.

sentences.zh: 複入為司成中大夫，典國史。

translations.literal: He again entered the capital as Grand Master of the Directorate of Education and oversaw the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as grand master of the directorate of education and oversaw the national history.

sentences.zh: 周代公卿，類多武將，唯羨以素業自通，甚為當時所重。

translations.literal: In the Zhou age the dukes and ministers were mostly military generals; only Xian made his way through pure scholarship and was greatly valued by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou ministers were mostly generals; Xian alone rose through scholarship and was highly esteemed in his day.

sentences.zh: 後以年老，致仕於家。

translations.literal: Later, because of old age, he retired to his home.
translations.idiomatic: He later retired at home due to age.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，欽其德望，以書征之曰：「朕初臨四海，思存政術，舊齒名賢，實懷勤佇。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, admiring his virtue and reputation, he summoned him by letter, saying, "We have just come to the four seas and think to preserve methods of government; old worthies and famed worthies—we truly harbor earnest longing.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, admiring his reputation, he summoned him by letter: "Having just come to rule the realm, I seek sound governance and earnestly long for venerable men of talent.

sentences.zh: 儀同昔在周室，德業有聞，雖雲致仕，猶克壯年。

translations.literal: Equipage, in former Zhou times your virtue and achievement were heard of; though you say you have retired, you are still in vigorous years.
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue was renowned under the Zhou; though you have retired, you are still in your prime.

sentences.zh: 即宜入朝，用副虛想。」

translations.literal: You should at once enter court to fulfill Our empty longing."
translations.idiomatic: Come to court at once to satisfy my eager hope.

sentences.zh: 及謁見，敕令勿拜，扶升殿，上降榻執手，與之同坐，宴語久之，賜以幾杖。

translations.literal: When he had audience, an edict ordered him not to bow; he was helped up the hall, the Emperor descended from the couch and took his hand, sat with him together, feasted and conversed for a long while, and granted him a staff and bench.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he was excused from bowing, helped up the hall, and the emperor descended to take his hand, sat with him, conversed at length over a feast, and gave him staff and bench.

sentences.zh: 會遷都龍首，羨上表勸以儉約，上優詔答之。

translations.literal: It happened that the capital was moved to Longshou; Xian submitted a memorial urging frugality, and the Emperor replied with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Longshou, Xian memorialized urging frugality, and the emperor replied with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 俄而卒，時年八十四。

translations.literal: Shortly he died, at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈滄州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Cang Province; his posthumous title was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Cang Province; his posthumous title was Ding.

sentences.zh: 撰《老子》、《莊子》義，名曰《道言》，五十二篇。

translations.literal: He compiled exegeses of the 《Laozi》 and 《Zhuangzi》, entitled 《The Way Spoken》, in fifty-two chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote exegeses of the 《Laozi》 and 《Zhuangzi》 entitled 《The Way Spoken》, in fifty-two chapters.

sentences.zh: 煚好學，有父風。

translations.literal: Jiong loved learning and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong loved learning and took after his father.

sentences.zh: 在魏釋褐奉朝請，遷員外侍郎。

translations.literal: In Wei, upon leaving the sackcloth he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance and was moved to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei he entered service as court gentleman for attendance and became vice director.

sentences.zh: 周太祖引為外兵曹。

translations.literal: The Zhou Founder drew him in as Outer Troops Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Founder appointed him to the outer troops bureau.

sentences.zh: 閔帝受禪，加前將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min received the abdication, Jiong was given the additional title of Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min took the throne, he was made forward general.

sentences.zh: 明、武世，曆膳部大夫、塚宰司錄，賜爵北平縣子，邑四百戶。

translations.literal: In the Ming and Wu reigns he passed through Grand Master of the Provisions Bureau and Recorder of the Grand Chancellor's Office, and was granted the title Viscount of Beiping County with a fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming and Wu emperors he served as grand master of the provisions bureau and recorder of the grand chancellor's office, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Beiping with four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，加儀同，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he was given Equipage and advanced in rank to Earl.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he was granted equipage and advanced to earl.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，煚深自推結，高祖以其有幹用，甚親遇之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Jiong deeply offered himself in alliance; Gaozu, because he had practical ability, treated him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor, Jiong pledged himself wholeheartedly; Gaozu valued his practical ability and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜尚書右丞，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Jiong was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and advanced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 俄遷太府少卿，領營新都監丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Vice Director of the Grand Treasury and oversaw the construction of the new capital as supervising director.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became vice director of the Grand Treasury and supervised construction of the new capital.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂去職，柴毀骨立。

translations.literal: He met his father's bereavement and left office, his emaciation from mourning leaving him skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father and was wasted to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 未期，起令視事，固讓不許，授儀同三司，襲爵虞鄉縣公，增邑通前千五百戶。

translations.literal: Before the mourning term ended he was raised and ordered to attend to affairs; he firmly declined but was not permitted, was granted General of the Third Rank with Equipage, inherited the title Duke of Yuxiang County, and his fief was increased to one thousand five hundred households in all with what came before.
translations.idiomatic: Before mourning ended he was recalled to duty despite his protests, granted third-rank honors, inherited the dukedom of Yuxiang, and his fief was increased to fifteen hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太府卿，拜民部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Director of the Grand Treasury and appointed Director of the Department of the People.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became director of the Grand Treasury and then director of the Department of the People.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣為揚州總管，授煚司馬，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Prince Guang of Jin was Grand Commander of Yang Province; Jiong was appointed Military Affairs Officer and given the additional title of Grand Master with Silver Seal and Green Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guang of Jin was grand commander of Yang Province, Jiong was made his military affairs officer with the honorific rank of grand master of the silver seal and green ribbon.

sentences.zh: 煚性和厚，有識度，甚有當時之譽。

translations.literal: Jiong by nature was harmonious and generous, with discernment and measure, and had a great reputation in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was good-natured and far-sighted and enjoyed high repute in his day.

sentences.zh: 後拜冀州刺史，晉王廣頻表請之，複為晉王長史，檢校蔣州事。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Ji Province; Prince Guang repeatedly memorialized requesting him and he again became the prince's Chief Clerk, inspecting affairs of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made governor of Ji Province; Prince Guang repeatedly requested him back and he again served as the prince's chief clerk, overseeing Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 及晉王為皇太子，複為冀州刺史，進位上開府，吏民悅服，稱為良二千石。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Jiong again became Governor of Ji Province, was advanced to Senior Opening the Office, and clerks and people were pleased and submitted—he was called a fine two-thousand-bushel official.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, Jiong again governed Ji Province, was advanced to senior opening the office, and won such loyalty from officials and people that he was called a model governor.

sentences.zh: 仁壽四年卒官，時年七十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Renshou he died in office, at age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the fourth year of Renshou, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 子慧寶，官至絳郡丞。

translations.literal: His son Huibao reached the office of Assistant Governor of Jiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huibao rose to assistant governor of Jiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇時有劉仁恩者，不知何許人也，倜儻有文武幹用。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era there was a Liu Ren'en, of unknown origin, bold and free with civil and martial practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era there was a Liu Ren'en of unknown origin, a man of bold spirit and both civil and martial talent.

sentences.zh: 初為毛州刺史，治績號天下第一，擢拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: At first he was Governor of Mao Province; his governing achievements were called first under Heaven, and he was promoted and appointed Director of the Department of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as governor of Mao Province, where his administration was ranked the best in the realm, and was promoted to director of the Department of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 又以行軍總管從楊素伐陳，與素破陳將呂仲肅于荊門，仁恩之計居多，授上大將軍，甚有當時之譽。

translations.literal: He also as Campaign Grand Commander followed Yang Su in attacking Chen; with Su he defeated the Chen general Lü Zhongsu at Jingmen—Ren'en's plans predominated—and he was granted Senior Grand General, with a great reputation in the age.
translations.idiomatic: As campaign commander he followed Yang Su against Chen and helped defeat the Chen general Lü Zhongsu at Jingmen, contributing most of the strategy; he was made senior grand general and won high renown.

sentences.zh: 馮翊郭均、上党馮世基，並明悟有幹略，相繼為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Guo Jun of Fufeng and Feng Shiji of Shangdang were both clear and perceptive with practical strategy and in succession were Directors of the Department of War.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jun of Fufeng and Feng Shiji of Shangdang were both sharp and capable administrators who served in succession as directors of the Department of War.

sentences.zh: 代人厙狄嶔，性弘厚，有局度，官至民部尚書。

translations.literal: Kudiji Qin of Dai by nature was broad and generous, with capacity and measure, and reached the office of Director of the Department of the People.
translations.idiomatic: Kudiji Qin of Dai was magnanimous and measured in character and rose to director of the Department of the People.

sentences.zh: 此四人俱顯名於當世，然事行闕落，史莫能詳。

translations.literal: These four men all had illustrious names in the age, yet their deeds and conduct are incomplete and fallen away, and the historians cannot detail them.
translations.idiomatic: These four were all famous in their day, but their deeds are poorly recorded and historians cannot tell their stories in full.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：二趙明習故事，當世所推，及居端右，無聞殊績。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The two Zhao were clear and practiced in precedent and were pushed by the age, yet when they occupied the top posts no special achievements were heard of.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The two Zhao were versed in precedent and highly regarded, yet in the highest offices they left no outstanding record.

sentences.zh: 固知人之才器，各有分限，大小異宜，不可逾量。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that men's talents and vessels each have their allotted limits; great and small differ in what is fitting and cannot be exceeded in measure.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that talent has its proper scope—great and small offices suit different men, and one cannot exceed a man's measure.

sentences.zh: 長孫平諫赦誹謗之罪，可謂仁人之言，高祖悅而從之，其利亦已博矣。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Ping's remonstrance to pardon the crime of slander can be called the words of a humane man; Gaozu was pleased and followed it—the benefit was already vast.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Ping's plea to pardon slanderers was the speech of a humane man; Gaozu gladly agreed, to the empire's great benefit.

sentences.zh: 元暉以明敏顯達，韋師以清白成名，楊尚希、楊異，宗室之英，譽望隆重，蘇孝慈、李雄、張煚，內外所履，鹹稱貞幹，並任開皇之初，蓋當時之選也。

translations.literal: Yuan Hui through clarity and keenness was illustrious and eminent; Wei Shi through incorruption made his name; Yang Shangxi and Yang Yi, elites of the imperial clan, had heavy reputation and esteem; Su Xiaoci, Li Xiong, and Zhang Jiong, in inner and outer posts they trod, were all called upright and capable—they all served at the beginning of Kaihuang and were roughly the choice of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hui rose through brilliance and acuity; Wei Shi won fame through integrity; Yang Shangxi and Yang Yi, outstanding among the imperial clan, enjoyed towering reputations; Su Xiaoci, Li Xiong, and Zhang Jiong were praised everywhere they served for steadfast competence—all held office at the dawn of Kaihuang and represented the finest men of their generation.
